item.title: The coming storm
item.description: As unavoidable as a hurricane. We must learn to fly into the eye.
item.dc:creator: djr
item.content:encoded: AI is deeply polarizing. In my last post that I put on LinkedIn, I tried to draw a line through where I think all of this is headed. I used a post from Addy, who just started working at Anthropic but has been something of an evangelist for a while. I see the contradiction, and I want to be clear about what I meant.

item.title: The conversation has shifted
item.description: From AI slop to Holy Shit!
item.dc:creator: djr
item.content:encoded: It became obvious once I saw Jeff Casimir share Harper Reed’s article on his CodeGen setup and dug in. This was last year. I tested the methodology on the spot and immediately saw the future we are staring down the barrel of. The last few months have been a whirlwind as the models have updated and seemingly shown their hand in response to viral phenomenon like OpenClaw. I personally have never been more productive and it is, honestly, keeping me up at night.

item.title: Just the beginning...
item.description: The world of technology is shifting beneath our feet.
item.dc:creator: djr
item.content:encoded: The world of technology is shifting beneath our feet. A space accustomed to disruption and uncertainty sure, but the emergence of AI has proven to be something else entirely. Not just solving a technical problem, it solves an intelligence problem at scale and has the potential to accelerate efforts across numerous industries. With this new method of computing comes a profound and for many often terrifying realization; are we prepared for what is beyond a horizon that is fast approaching?
